To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the velocity field structure and evolution of the high-Reynolds number free shear layer are significantly different than those of lower Reynolds number flows.

the velocity field structure of a two-stream turbulent planar free shear layers at a Reynolds number of about 2.6 x 10 4 is characterized by agglomerated vorticities of both signs and that the evolution of this structure is significantly different from that of a passive scalar.

the two-dimensional velocity field in a high Reynolds number turbulent free shear layer is dominated by complex, three-dimensional vortical structures, and these vortices are characterized by a wide distribution of convective velocities.

the velocity field structure of a high Reynolds number free shear layer was characterized by a highly agglomerated, three-dimensional, complex, and noncoherent vortex system.
the shear layer was a complex, three-dimensional, time-evolving flow with a highly variable velocity and vorticity structure.
the shear layer is a complex, highly turbulent, spatially incoherent, and temporally evolving structure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the high-Reynolds number free shear layer is a very complex three-dimensional flow with significant temporal variation and that it is not well described by the passive scalar field.
the high-Reynolds number free shear layer is a highly complex, turbulent flow field.
the velocity and vorticity field structures were highly complex and time dependent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the shear layer is not simply a collection of well-defined vortices, but rather an agglomerated collection of vortices that are not well defined.
the flow is much less ordered than previously thought and that the flow is more three dimensional than previously thought.
the velocity and passive scalar fields in a high Reynolds number free shear layer are not simply related by a linear transformation.
